answer: No. Your records show you did not have a blood clot in your lung. On 8 July 2025 you had chest pain and a blood test called D-dimer, which was raised at 0.92 (normal is 0.49 or less). A raised D-dimer can be a sign of a clot, but it is not specific and often goes up for other reasons. You then had a CT scan of the chest with contrast dye, which is the standard test for a lung clot. The report says there was no pulmonary embolism, your lungs were clear, and there was no fluid around the lungs or heart. The only finding was mild age-related wear in the spine of your upper back. Your records list pulmonary embolism as ruled out, and the chest pain was recorded as chest wall pain, which settled by 22 July 2025.
short: A chest CT angiogram on 8 July 2025, done for chest pain with a raised D-dimer, showed no pulmonary embolism. The diagnosis was ruled out, and the pain was attributed to the chest wall and resolved by 22 July 2025.
